title: not a fan of liquid reservoir in head, or the wringer, but otherwise same as all others
text:
not a fan of liquid reservoir in head, or the wringer, but otherwise same as all others. I have had a few batteries free spray mops. Love them, but some are better for me over others. My go to is still [[ASIN:B07N1SY964 Amazon Basics Spray Mop]] which I have been using since 2019, so nearly 3 years. It is of less price, and I think has a better design than this one. I dont rate on price as we can all see the price, prices fluctuate (especially now), we all have different budgets, values, and needs. So the current "sale" price of $37 is rather high even for me. But you do you. Shop around.

As for how it works-- it is ok. It works. Nothing all that negative sticks out to me. I wasn't sure what I would think of the liquid reservoir being IN the main head. I know now that I dont care for that. I can't see when I am getting low. It holds a cup of liquid, which is actually PLENTY to do a wide floor area, and can last many many cleanings for spot cleaning. I have had a few different spray mops, and most hold 1.5 cups, and I always get several cleanings out of a fill up. I guess it depends on WHAT you use, and how much you use. I always start with a damp cleaning pad.

Perfectly fine for any floor. It is just a micro fiber mop head. You use your own cleaner.

Mop head is pretty standard, and I find that I can use this mop pad on other spray mops, or use other mop pads on this. No surprises here.

Has same spray (fine) as others, has same easy to engage spray handle. The main difference is where the water reservoir (in head versus further up pole). Has same rotation. Has same slim profile and ease of storage. I find out of the 3-4 spray mops I have used that they are nearly all the same. One of the few things that can be purchased based on price. But for my preference the Amazon one has been my consistent go to.

The "stand out" feature is the ability to wring it out using a slider. I find that I dont use it. I find that I prefer to take the mop pad off and wring it out in the sink, then after I am done for the day I toss in the washer. I find that it is more annoying then helpful. By the way, I clean homes for a living, and using this feels like an extra step.

SO OVERALL- its fine. I think it is "OK". Not great, not bad. Middle of road rating of 3. I simply find the extra features to be not so extra. In fact, I find them a little annoying. But you may love it. Some stuff simply comes down to preference.
